summary: Ustaz Azlan describes the moral breakdown of jahili Arab society that the Prophet SAW saw before prophethood, beginning with the hadith that he was sent to perfect good character and Ja'far's speech before the Negus summing up that jahiliyyah. He covers materialism, alcohol and gambling, corrupt forms of marriage, slavery and the killing of baby girls, and links each to today. The second half tells the story of Zayd ibn Harithah: kidnapped, sold at Ukaz, bought by Hakim ibn Hizam, given to Khadijah and then to the Prophet SAW, choosing to stay with him over returning to his father, and being declared his son.
keyPoints: The Prophet SAW was sent to perfect good character; character is the output that shows the right input of belief and process of worship.
Ja'far summed up jahiliyyah before the Negus: idol worship, eating carrion, shameful deeds, cutting kinship ties, harming neighbours and the strong devouring the weak.
Jahiliyyah meant materialism, addiction to alcohol and gambling, corrupt marriages, slavery and burying baby girls, all of which still exist in other forms today.
A Muslim must take notice and act against such evils even when they happen among non-Muslims.
Zayd ibn Harithah, an Arab boy kidnapped and sold as a slave, was given by Khadijah to the Prophet SAW.
Zayd chose to stay with the Prophet SAW even when his father came to redeem him, so the Prophet SAW freed him and declared him his son before the Kaaba.

lessons.title: Character is the output of Islam
lessons.body: If character is still lacking, check the input of belief and the process of worship.

lessons.title: Listen before judging
lessons.body: The Negus heard accusation and defence first; we should not accept labels without hearing.

lessons.title: Modern idols
lessons.body: Position, status, lineage and a bank account can become things we worship.

lessons.title: Watch what you eat
lessons.body: Manufactured food today can be like 'carrion' from a health point of view.

lessons.title: Materialism is countered by Al-Kahf and At-Takathur
lessons.body: The stories of Surah Al-Kahf are an antibody against materialism.

lessons.title: Pleasant names for the forbidden
lessons.body: Forbidden things are often given nice names, like alcohol called 'karam'.

lessons.title: Empathy for those struggling with addiction
lessons.body: The ruling does not loosen, but we can understand a new Muslim's struggle with a long addiction.

lessons.title: Beware deviant sects in Islamic dress
lessons.body: Handing wives to a leader marks deviant groups even when they dress and speak like Islam.

lessons.title: Jahiliyyah returns in new forms
lessons.body: Partner swapping, mistresses and prostitution still exist on different platforms.

lessons.title: Muslims must act against evil
lessons.body: Do not say 'let them be, they are disbelievers'; we must take notice and act against injustice.

lessons.title: Love that shapes a choice
lessons.body: Zayd stayed because of the love he had never felt from anyone else.

lessons.title: Respect the birth parents' rights
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW left the decision to Zayd, asked for no payment, and understood the father's grief.

glossary.meaning: Ignorance of knowledge and of emotion, not based on facts and driven by tribal feelings.
Carrion, an animal that died without being slaughtered.
A pleasant name given to alcohol because it was linked to generosity.
Gambling, linked to the ease of getting money.
Secret marriage, or the practice of keeping mistresses.
A son named after another man; in Arab custom a kind of lineage upgrade, later changed by Surah Al-Ahzab.

dalil.context: The basis for saying that character is Islam's output.
dalil.translation: I was sent only to perfect good character.

dalil.context: Mentioned as Ibn Abbas's report in Sahih Bukhari.
dalil.translation: If you want to know the moral collapse of the Arabs of jahiliyyah, read from verse 130 of Surah Al-An'am onwards.

dalil.context: Ibn Abbas told people to read verse 130 onwards of Al-An'am to learn the ugliness of jahili Arabs.
dalil.translation: ‘Company of jinn and mankind! Did messengers not come from among you to recite My revelations to you and warn that you would meet this Day?’ They will say, ‘We testify against ourselves.’ The life of this world seduced them, but they will testify against themselves that they rejected the truth:

dalil.context: The verse that rebukes boasting in accumulating wealth. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
The ustaz reads visiting the graves as boasting about dead rich people. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: until you go into your graves.

dalil.context: Surah Al-Kahf is presented as a remedy for materialism.
dalil.translation: Whoever reads Surah Al-Kahf, it becomes a light for him between two Fridays; memorising its first ten verses protects against tribulation.

dalil.context: The verse on alcohol and gambling that says there is great sin and some benefit, during the staged prohibition.
dalil.translation: They ask you [Prophet] about intoxicants and gambling: say, ‘There is great sin in both, and some benefit for people: the sin is greater than the benefit.’ They ask you what they should give: say, ‘Give what you can spare.’ In this way, God makes His messages clear to you, so that you may reflect

dalil.context: Allah SWT commands that adopted sons be called by their fathers' names.
dalil.translation: Name your adopted sons after their real fathers: this is more equitable in God’s eyes––if you do not know who their fathers are [they are your] ‘brothers-in-religion’ and proteges. You will not be blamed if you make a mistake, only for what your hearts deliberately intend; God is most forgiving and merciful.
